result.topic_en: The page sketches an argument about expanding roots in rational series and states theorems that algebraic functions taking rational values at all rational (or positive integer) arguments must be rational functions. It then lists possible kinds of continuity and discontinuity for a function of a real variable, with an example.

items.english: Theorem I: If an algebraic function of x has the property of being rational for all rational values of x between α and β, then it is necessarily a rational function of x with rational number coefficients.

items.quote:
Satz II ———— alle ganzen positiven Werte von $x$ rational zu sein, so
ist sie nothwendig eine rationale Funktion von $x$ mit rationalen Zahlcoefficienten.
items.english: Theorem II: (If an algebraic function of x has the property,) for all positive integer values of x, of being rational, then it is necessarily a rational function of x with rational number coefficients.

items.english: On the concept of continuity of a function of a real variable: it is possible to be 0) continuous everywhere; 1) continuous everywhere, discontinuous at one point; 2) discontinuous everywhere, continuous at one point; 3) discontinuous on an everywhere-dense point set, otherwise continuous.
